title: Solar Al appendix

products.stat_basis: quantiser-floor 0.01 dex (RYA-771) — UNMEASURED: line-to-line scatter at n_lines=1; the floor STANDS IN for a scatter that was never determined, it is not a measurement of one

components.name: measurement
components.source: Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1: one line -> statistical error from the goodness of the profile fit; chi2-curvature sigma of this line, rescaled to red_chi2 = 1

evidence.likelihood: synthesis chi2 over the fit window, curvature at the best abundance
evidence.correlation_treatment: red_chi2 rescaling absorbs pixel correlation and model inadequacy; the worse-constrained side is taken

components.name: transition_data
components.source: gf covariance per data/reference/gf_error_model.csv -- AL_AGSS21: fully_correlated (scale 0.0000 dex; Nordlander & Lind 2017 A&A 607 A75 Table A.1 + Sect. 2.1.2; Burheim, Hartman & Nilsson 2023 A&A 672 A197 Table 3)

components.name: stellar.logg
components.source: solar log g is pinned; delta_logg is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.metallicity
components.source: solar [Fe/H] is pinned; delta_feh is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.teff
components.source: sourced DEFINED zero (RYA-1226 convention): the solar Teff allowance is 1 K

evidence.owed_measurement: a Teff perturbation on this pool

components.name: model_atmosphere
components.source: Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1: half the mean (<3D> - Holweger & Mueller 1974) (+) half the mean (3D - <3D>), per-line LTE abundances of Scott+2015 I/II (pool lines, n=1)

components.name: blends
components.source: full atomic + molecular synthesis in-window (RYA-1230 turned molecular opacity on in every band); no catalogued-blend deficit

evidence.owed_measurement: a paired molecule-strength leg on this C/O pool

components.name: nlte
components.source: this leg applies no departures (nlte_delta_dex = 0 on every line)

components.name: pseudo_continuum
components.source: outside the near-UV the continuum is observed; it is placed per line by the standing rule and priced on `continuum`

components.name: hfs_isotopes
components.source: modelled: every hyperfine-split pool line is synthesised component by component from the band's synthesis list (lab HFS; as RYA-466/473 Cu, V, Mn and RYA-1217 Al); Asplund+2021 carries no HFS term

components.name: molecular_coupling
components.source: atomic product; the selector is not a MOL- indicator set

components.name: holding_instrument
components.source: SynthesisHandler harness residual MEASURED against the known optical answer (RYA-869)

components.name: stellar.xi
components.source: not in the Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1 budget (stat, atmosphere, half the 3D effect, NLTE); RYA-1315 runs only those legs

components.name: continuum
components.source: not in the Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1 budget (stat, atmosphere, half the 3D effect, NLTE); RYA-1315 runs only those legs

components.name: profile_ew
components.source: not in the Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1 budget (stat, atmosphere, half the 3D effect, NLTE); RYA-1315 runs only those legs

components.name: telluric
components.source: not in the Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1 budget (stat, atmosphere, half the 3D effect, NLTE); RYA-1315 runs only those legs

uncertainty.covariance_source: components independent of one another; the shared-source gf correlation lives inside transition_data
uncertainty.assumptions: solar log g and [Fe/H] pinned; Teff allowance 1 K

body_html:
Solar aluminium: 6.541 ± 0.037

Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse 2021: 6.43 ± 0.03  ·  this measurement +0.111 dex

Measured the way Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse (2021) measure it: the Asplund et al. 2021 line set (Nordlander & Lind 2017: the Al I lines of their Table A.1), 6 lines measured on one spectrum, each part weighted by its uncertainty.

  • Al I: 6.516 ± 0.037 · Kitt Peak (1984, molecfit) · VIS · Al I · Asplund et al. 2021 lines · <3D> LTE (Gerber)
  • Al I: 6.521 ± 0.051 · Kitt Peak (1984, molecfit) · red-optical · Al I · Asplund et al. 2021 lines · <3D> LTE (Gerber)
  • Al I: 6.591 ± 0.044 · Kitt Peak (1984, molecfit) · NIR · Al I · Asplund et al. 2021 lines · <3D> LTE (Gerber)

Line grades

Every product is measured on one of three grades of spectral lines and the grades are never mixed in one number.

Scroll horizontally to read all columns · focus the table and use the arrow keys

Line grades
GradeWhat it meansThis element
Reference Gradelines from a published solar line set (Asplund et al. 2021 and similar), measured with the oscillator strengths the authors used46 products -- Al I · Asplund et al. 2021 lines
Codex Gradelines chosen by the Codex whose oscillator strength carries a published uncertainty (laboratory measurement, NIST accuracy class A-C, or the paper's own stated error), between 5% and 60% deep40 products -- Al I · Codex-graded lines
Deep Gradethe same oscillator-strength rule on lines deeper than 60% -- stronger lines, more sensitive to damping and the model atmospherenone for the Sun: every line in this grade is excluded as saturated or an outlier (see Excluded lines)

How to read this forest. Each row is one independent product, preserving its band, holding, engine, indicator and line set. Engines and indicator families are never averaged. Each bar is the uncertainty as Asplund et al. 2021 quote it: line-to-line scatter, the 3D-model term and the NLTE term (at least 0.03 dex). For a molecule the NLTE term is replaced by its dependence on the other element, and the 3D term comes from the 3D-to-1D difference Amarsi et al. 2021 publish for the same band. Atomic-data and observational terms are not in the bar, as in Asplund; they stay in the full error budget attached to the row. Grades describe the supplied line-pool provenance, not engine quality; evaluated theoretical CNO oscillator strengths are not relabelled as laboratory evidence. Quarantined, failed and unconstrained fits have no abundance mark. Experimental products remain explicitly not adopted. Literature references provide context, never tuning targets.

How this was measured

Every aluminium value on this page comes from fitting synthetic spectra to the observed solar spectrum, line by line or band by band, with the aluminium abundance as the free parameter. The synthesis includes the atomic lines and the molecular opacity in every window, so blended absorption is modelled rather than attributed to the line being measured. The continuum is placed locally around every line by comparing the observation with the synthesis on its own highest pixels, and ground-based spectra are telluric-corrected across their full range.

Each indicator is measured independently on each solar spectrum and reported separately; nothing is averaged across indicators or instruments. Where a 3D or NLTE correction is published for the lines, it is applied as its own product (1D-LTE, 1D-NLTE and 3D-NLTE are separate rows). Every value carries a full uncertainty budget: fit, line strengths, microturbulence, continuum, fit window, model atmosphere, telluric residual, and the spread between spectra, each measured by refitting with that one input changed. The headline at the top is the Asplund-grade product: a published line set, the most complete treatment, then the most lines.

Solar aluminium context

Aluminium is traced by Al I lines in the optical and near-infrared. The reference lines are the six Asplund et al. 2021 used (Nordlander & Lind 2017: 6696, 6698, 7835, 8912, 10768 and 10872 Å) with the oscillator strengths and uncertainties those authors adopted. Al I departs from LTE, so each spectrum also carries a non-LTE-corrected product; each set, spectrum and treatment remains a separate product.
